participation.context: Heard the message, refused the further question, and did not sit down to a copy.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Delivered the sentence as he was given it, filled the rest with words, and asked for the proverb before a printer.
participation.name: John Florio

relations.note: the paper received, and nothing more
relations.quote: I say it as he said it.

story.body: You took the call at eleven, heard the one sentence from my lord, and did not ask for another. You left the proverb uncopied. You did not invent a reply he had not sent.

relations.note: the paper received, and nothing more
relations.quote: I say it as he said it.

title: Heard that the paper was received

participation.context: Wrote the note and left both the proverb and the chair where the morning had put them.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: nothing more asked after the one sentence

story.body: You set down Florio's sentence and your refusal to ask past it. You did not make a fair copy for a printer. You noted the chair in the same breath and started no new work from either.
